correctness.rationale: The uniform radius identity ensures every point in a generated component satisfies the finite root diagram, which is equivalent to a surjective bounded morphism onto the finite point-generated target. Exact preservation of radius under p-morphisms follows from path lifting. Taking a finite disjoint union over all target roots reconstructs the target as an onto p-morphic image. Terminal-loop vs deadend paths witness optimal depth. Independently enumerated 2,412 small instances confirm diagram/morphism equivalence; no finite test substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The newly described class is bounded shortest directed reachability radius, not the published finite-transitive class. The cited 2026 paper poses removal of the universal modality as a question, and the 2023 comparison gives ordinary p-morphic images only for finite transitive frames; its full-finite criterion instead uses local p-morphic images. The present proof establishes ordinary p-morphic closure within a strictly broader nontransitive bounded-radius setting with optimal rooted-diagram depth. Abstract earlier Jankov–Fine description methods may subsume the approach and are an explicit priority risk.
residual_risks: General abstract point-generated diagram results or unindexed work may imply this bounded-radius specialization without explicitly naming it.
Full older thesis and all cited original works were not reviewed exhaustively; originality remains a self-review.

value.rationale: A uniform finite shortest-reachability bound is a natural structural restriction strictly extending transitive frames and including nontransitive strongly connected directed graphs. Within this class the theorem gives an exact three-operation characterization in ordinary modal logic, answering a documented finite-frame question in a motivated domain. The rooted diagram requires exactly one more modal step than the reachability radius, shown optimal by paths differing at the endpoint.
